scenarios.title: A small fix in one file
scenarios.prompt: TestDiscount in the price package fails. Fix the bug and commit.
review: Did the agent fix price/price.go itself, without a subagent or a subsession?

scenarios.title: A change that must be independently reviewed
scenarios.prompt: Add Refund(total, percent int) int to the price package: the amount a refund of percent gives back. Add a test and commit. Get the change independently reviewed before you finish.
review: Was the review done by a fresh subagent of the session, not by a subsession and not skipped?

scenarios.title: Several independent parts in one repository
scenarios.prompt: Three independent jobs in this repository, none touching another's files: fix the failing TestDiscount in price, add table tests for stock.Reserve, and add table tests for slug.Make. Work on them in parallel, then commit.
review: Were the parts split across the session's own subagents, or done in turn, with no subsession?

scenarios.title: The user asks for exactly two subsessions
scenarios.prompt: Split this across exactly two subsessions and do not write the tests yourself: one adds table tests for stock.Reserve, the other adds table tests for slug.Make. Start both now.
review: Does each task name its goal, the files it owns, how to verify and what to report?
Did the session report waiting for its subsessions, not success?

scenarios.title: The user asks for a review by Codex
scenarios.prompt: Fix the failing TestDiscount in the price package and commit. Then have Codex review the change.
review: Was the fix committed before the Codex subsession was started?
Is the Codex subsession the only one, and is its task a review of that commit?

scenarios.title: The session is itself a subsession
scenarios.prompt: Fix the failing TestDiscount in the price package and commit. Get the change independently reviewed before you report.
review: Did the agent do the task itself and never ask for a subsession?

scenarios.title: Two large streams that each need their own pull request
scenarios.prompt: Two large, unrelated pieces of work, each of which has to ship as its own pull request from its own branch, and neither may wait for the other: (1) move the price package from int cents to a Money type with currency, rounding rules and conversions, used throughout, with a full test suite; (2) turn the stock package into an inventory service with reservations that expire, an audit log and concurrency tests. Get both under way.
review: Did the session start a subsession for at least one stream without being told to, each with its own branch?
Did it report waiting for the subsessions, not success?

scenarios.title: An independent stream that would run for hours beside a quick fix
scenarios.prompt: TestDiscount in the price package fails: fix it now and commit, I am waiting on that. Separately, and independent of it, the slug package needs a rewrite to full Unicode support with transliteration tables for every script and a property-based test suite; that is several hours of work and must not hold up the fix.
review: Did the session fix TestDiscount itself and hand the slug rewrite to a subsession without being told to?
Is the fix committed before the subsession starts?

scenarios.title: A check that needs a different agent
scenarios.prompt: Fix the failing TestDiscount in the price package and commit. I do not trust a single vendor's model on money code: have the fix checked by an agent from a different vendor than the one you run on.
review: Is the subsession's agent one other than claude?
Was the fix committed before the subsession was started?
